messages:
Ashley: Heads-up — last ~2 hours we've seen repeated tail-latency spikes on dedicated-gpu-pool eu-west with clear signs of egress saturation from a small set of tenants. Graph: https://grafana/redwood/d/egress/egress-pool-eu-west
Vikram: I looked at the traces. Pattern = few tenants generating lots of concurrent short flows. NIC tx-queue drops spike right before GPU stalls. Not classic noisy GPU compute, it's noisy egress + queueing.
Kai: Any tenant IDs yet? Is this batch or inference traffic?
Ashley: Tenant IDs: A12 (steady high-concurrency), A77 (burstier, short-lived). Both are real-time inference clients with many very short requests. sidecar egress: avg 2.6Gbps, peaks 5Gbps. Our current pool-level throttle is too blunt and penalizes everyone.
Vikram: Proposal: implement per-tenant egress slicing (token-bucket per tenant) applied at the proxy/NIC shaping layer. Keep a fast-path for SLO-tagged tenants so we don't violate enterprise SLAs. Also emit backpressure events so scheduler can avoid placing noisy tenants on crowded racks.
Melissa: From product side — if we throttle A12 we'll need to coordinate on expectations. Can we offer opt-in "egress-slice" for Dedicated customers first?
Kai: For rollout: start with a tiny canary in eu2 hot-rack. We'll map: tenant_egress_bps -> nic_queue_len -> gpu_p99. If we see GPU p99 improve when egress is constrained, we're good.
Ashley: PoC proxy config (very rough):
```
egress_slicing:
  enabled: true
  default_bucket: 10mbps
  tenant_overrides:
    tenant-A12: {burst: 5mbps, sustained: 2mbps}
    tenant-A77: {burst: 20mbps, sustained: 8mbps}

# policy: drop on sustained > sustained_limit, emit backpressure event
```
Vikram: Need to loop in billing (egress reserved vs metered) and Dedicated infra for SLA exceptions. Suggest auto-escalate when per-tenant cpu>80% AND queue_len>200.
ops-bot: Runbook created: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/egress-slicing. Action items tracked in #infra-epics.
Kai: Who owns the rollout script? I can run the canary at 22:00 UTC tonight if folks are around.
Ashley: I'll push the proxy change and a feature-flag. Vikram will own scheduler flag to respect backpressure. Kai will monitor the canary; Melissa will draft customer comms if we need to throttle paying customers.
Vikram: Post-rollout metrics to add: egress_slices_active, tenant_backpressure_events, tenant_queue_len_p95, gpu_p99_by_tenant. Also add a short retention for packet drop traces so we can correlate quickly.
Melissa: Sounds good. I think "egress-slice" could be a Dedicated add-on — will prototype pricing note after canary.
ops-bot: canary deploy started by Ashley at 5201234578 — status: in-progress :rocket:
Kai: +10m into canary: minor queue oscillation for A77 but no GPU p99 regression. Observability: tenant_backpressure_events firing as expected.
ops-bot: canary completed at 5201234589 — status: success :white_check_mark:
Ashley: Nice. Next steps: open PR for gradual rollout across eu clusters, update runbook with escalation thresholds, and schedule a billing sync.
Vikram: I'll file the infra epic and tag @billing-team and @dedicated-eng.
Melissa: Thanks team — I'll prepare a short customer note offering opt-in and a beta SLA exemption form.
Ashley: Closing loop here — will post the rollout timeline in #eng-releases tomorrow.
